title: Marine Engineers and Naval Architects
description: Design, develop, and evaluate the operation of marine vessels, ship machinery, and related equipment, such as power supply and propulsion systems.

tasks.text: Design layout of craft interior, including cargo space, passenger compartments, ladder wells, and elevators.
Prepare, or direct the preparation of, product or system layouts and detailed drawings and schematics.
Design and oversee testing, installation, and repair of marine apparatus and equipment.
Determine conditions under which tests are to be conducted, as well as sequences and phases of test operations.
Maintain contact with, and formulate reports for, contractors and clients to ensure completion of work at minimum cost.
Prepare technical reports for use by engineering, management, or sales personnel.
Maintain records of engineering department activities, including expense records and details of equipment maintenance and repairs.

clusters.label: Judging the Qualities of Objects, Services, or People

tasks.text: Conduct analyses of ships, such as stability, structural, weight, and vibration analyses.
Evaluate performance of craft during dock and sea trials to determine design changes and conformance with national and international standards.
Evaluate operation of marine equipment during acceptance testing and shakedown cruises.
Check, test, and maintain automatic controls and alarm systems.
Inspect marine equipment and machinery to draw up work requests and job specifications.
Conduct environmental, operational, or performance tests on marine machinery and equipment.
Study design proposals and specifications to establish basic characteristics of craft, such as size, weight, speed, propulsion, displacement, and draft.
Conduct analytical, environmental, operational, or performance studies to develop designs for products, such as marine engines, equipment, and structures.
Review work requests and compare them with previous work completed on ships to ensure that costs are economically sound.
Perform monitoring activities to ensure that ships comply with international regulations and standards for life-saving equipment and pollution preventatives.
Investigate and observe tests on machinery and equipment for compliance with standards.

clusters.label: Drafting, Laying Out, and Specifying Technical Devices, Parts, and Equipment

tasks.text: Design complete hull and superstructure according to specifications and test data, in conformity with standards of safety, efficiency, and economy.
Establish arrangement of boiler room equipment and propulsion machinery, heating and ventilating systems, refrigeration equipment, piping, and other functional equipment.
Supervise other engineers and crew members and train them for routine and emergency duties.
Coordinate activities with regulatory bodies to ensure repairs and alterations are at minimum cost and consistent with safety.
Act as liaisons between ships' captains and shore personnel to ensure that schedules and budgets are maintained, and that ships are operated safely and efficiently.
Maintain and coordinate repair of marine machinery and equipment for installation on vessels.
Oversee construction and testing of prototype in model basin and develop sectional and waterline curves of hull to establish center of gravity, ideal hull form, and buoyancy and stability data.
Procure materials needed to repair marine equipment and machinery.
Schedule machine overhauls and the servicing of electrical, heating, ventilation, refrigeration, water, and sewage systems.
Prepare plans, estimates, design and construction schedules, and contract specifications, including any special provisions.
Analyze data to determine feasibility of product proposals.
Confer with research personnel to clarify or resolve problems and to develop or modify designs.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Science
skills.def: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Operation and Control
skills.def: Controlling operations of equipment or systems.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: AeroHydro MultiSurf, Autodesk AutoCAD, Bentley STAAD, Dassault Systemes SolidWorks.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: IBM Lotus 1-2-3, Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: McNeel Rhinoceros 3D.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: ANSYS AQWA, ANSYS ASAS, Ansys Fluent, Autodesk Algor Simulation.
